title: Case 23 races the wall clock and goes red under a loaded runner
body:
## Summary
tools/engines-rules-test.cjs case 23 asserted the parallel live check finished in under 120 ms against a 160 ms serial sum. That is a timing race, so the case went red whenever the machine was busy.

## Description
The case proved "side by side" with `took<120` (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs:291 before the fix) over four 40 ms stubs. A busy runner stretches every timer. The director measured 307 ms under the parallel run-rules load, and the case passed when run alone. The fix is test-harness/flake-lifecycle (fix the cause, never delete the test). The stubs now count runs in flight (`n.peak`), and the case asserts peak 4. All four runs start in microtasks before any 40 ms timer can fire, so the figure does not depend on load. The `row.ms>=30` lower bound stays, because load can only raise it.

## Flow
- 32 suite processes x 2 rounds beside 20 CPU burners (scratch harness load23.cjs) -> case 23 red in 52 of 64 runs ("parallel: 134..203 ms")
- fix: stubAll counts runs in flight; case 23 asserts peak === 4
- seeded control: engineCheck made serial -> red, "peak 1"; reverted

## Expected impact
The director's integration gate stops reporting a false red on the engines suite. A real regression to serial live checks still fails, and the seed proves it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the parallel claim is pinned by a count, not a race
Before: red in 52 of 64 runs under load (32 concurrent x 2, 20 burners); green alone
After: red in 0 of 64 under the same load; seeded serial engineCheck red with peak 1
Method: gate - the same load harness on both sides, plus the seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none

title: fit() counts UTF-16 units where the schema check counts characters
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts fit() refused strings that the schema check had just accepted. The cause was that the two count length in different units.

## Description
validate() counts maxLength in characters (`[...value].length`, desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts:44). fit() used `value.length`, which counts UTF-16 units. Linga holds a reply to str(230) (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:43) and then to line(reply, 230) (conversation.ts:29). So a 230-character reply with one emoji passed the schema, never triggered the shorten re-ask, and was then refused as "does not fit the screen". Fixed: fit() counts characters, the same way validate() does.

## Flow
- tutor reply = 229 letters + 1 emoji -> validate() passes -> line() throws -> the turn fails
- fix: `[...value].length > max` in fit()

## Expected impact
A Linga turn no longer fails on an answer that the contract accepted. A string one character over the limit is still refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one length rule, two call sites that agree
Before: fit refuses a 230-char, 231-unit string that validate accepts (sweep case 1 red)
After: fit accepts it; 231 chars still refused (sweep case 1 green); linga-rules-test 110/110
Method: gate - red-then-green test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts:22 (before) `value.length > max`
desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts:44 `const n = [...value].length;`
desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:29,43 line(...,230) vs reply:str(230)

title: findBinary reports an extensionless npm shim as installed on Windows
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts findBinary() searched for a bare name with no extension on Windows. A spawn without a shell never does that, so the engine probe said "installed" for a binary that could not start.

## Description
types.ts:61-62 says findBinary searches "the way a spawn without a shell does". On Windows, libuv tries a name as it is only when the name already has an extension, then tries .com and .exe. findBinary tried "" first, so `C:\nvm4w\nodejs\codex` (npm's sh shim, next to codex.cmd) counted as found. spawn("codex") on that machine is ENOENT, which a scratch probe reproduced.

## Flow
- codex.js not found -> codexCli.probe falls back to findBinary("codex") -> sh shim -> "codex is installed" -> the call fails ENOENT
- fix: on win32, try "" only when the name has an extension, then .com and .exe

## Expected impact
The engine check stops saying "codex is installed" when it cannot start. claude.exe and piper.exe resolve as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the probe predicts the spawn
Before: findBinary("codex") = C:\nvm4w\nodejs\codex (spawn ENOENT); sweep case 2 red
After: null; claude/piper .exe unchanged; sweep case 2 green
Method: gate - red-then-green test, plus a probe on this machine's PATH
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts:69 (before) `["", ".exe", ".com"]`
node spawn("fakebin") with an extensionless file on PATH -> error ENOENT
PATH scan: codex "" C:\nvm4w\nodejs\codex; codex ".cmd" ...codex.cmd

title: listen reports any non-ElevenLabs transcriber as on this machine
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/listen.ts set `local = !cloud()`. So a LAN or hosted STT_URL counted as local, and the engine check told the operator that the audio stayed on this machine.

## Description
The rule for capture in listen.ts:6-9 is that nothing leaves the machine unless someone chooses it. listenStatus() (listen.ts:34,36 before the fix) derived local from "not api.elevenlabs.io", and the probe said "<provider> answers on this machine." for http://192.168.1.20:8080. Fixed: local means a loopback host (localhost, 127.x, [::1]). The unreachable wording now keys on cloud(), so a remote whisper box that is down still gets "start gravitone, or set STT_URL".

## Flow
- STT_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8080 -> listenStatus().local true -> probe "answers on this machine."
- fix: onThisMachine() reads the URL hostname

## Expected impact
The operator stops being told that audio stays local when it does not. Nothing changes for the default localhost setup.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the capture claim matches where the audio goes
Before: 2 of 2 non-loopback URLs reported local and "on this machine"
After: 0 of 2; 3 of 3 loopback hosts still local (sweep case 3)
Method: gate - red-then-green test with stubbed fetch
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/listen.ts:34,36 (before) `local: !cloud()`
desk/src/lib/engines/listen.ts:55 `s.local ? `${s.provider} answers on this machine.``

title: Shape rule ignores minimum/maximum though it claims the desk's whole subset
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts says its validator covers "exactly the JSON-schema subset the desk writes". The desk writes minimum and maximum, and the validator did not check either.

## Description
items.ts writes `pieces {minimum:2,maximum:10}` (desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:190) and `difficulty {minimum:1,maximum:5}` (items.ts:224). validate() skipped both, so validate(9, difficulty) returned []. It now checks them. In-tree behaviour does not change, because the only schema with these keywords is held through the looser CALC_ACCEPT (items.ts:229,253).

## Flow
- validate(9,{type:"integer",minimum:1,maximum:5}) -> [] before; one break after

## Expected impact
The doc becomes true, and the next caller that holds a numeric range through `schema` alone gets it enforced. Calc suites stay green.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated subset matches the checked subset
Before: number keywords written 2, checked 0 (sweep case 4 red)
After: checked 2 of 2 (green); calc2-approx and calc-course green
Method: gate - red-then-green test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts:6-8 doc
git grep minimum: -> desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:190, :224 (only sites)

title: embed() accepts ragged vectors that score NaN in cosine()
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/embed.ts checked the vector count and element type, but not that all vectors in an answer had one length.

## Description
embed() (embed.ts:37 before the fix) let [[1,0,0],[1,0]] resolve. cosine() (embed.ts:42-46) then reads past the short vector and returns NaN, a score that library/lessons ranks without refusing it. Fixed: every vector must match the first one's length, or the call fails with EngineError("shape").

## Flow
- provider answers ragged -> embed resolves -> bestWindow scores NaN
- fix: x.length === v[0].length

## Expected impact
A broken embedding answer surfaces as the typed shape error at the engine instead of a silent NaN rank. 18 suites that stub embed stay green.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one shape rule for vectors
Before: ragged answer resolves (sweep case 5 red)
After: EngineError shape; even answers unchanged (green; 18 embed-stubbing suites green)
Method: gate - red-then-green test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/embed.ts:37 (before) no length check
cosine([1,0,0],[1,0]) -> NaN

title: Case 20 cannot see a serial status round it claims to pin
body:
## Summary
tools/engines-rules-test.cjs case 20 claims "the round is parallel", but its stub probes answered at once, so a serial engineStatus() also passed.

## Description
Case 20 has four instant probes plus one that never answers, under a 30 ms budget, and asserts <500 ms. Serial rounds finish in about 40 ms, so the case cannot fail on the defect it names. The pass is coverage theater (test-harness/negative-control-tests). The probes now answer only once all five have started, so asked one at a time the first one runs past the budget and is not ok.

## Flow
- seed: engineStatus made serial -> case 20 green (before)
- fix: probes released by an all-five-started promise
- same seed -> red "text: ... did not answer in 30 ms" (after); reverted

## Expected impact
A regression to a serial status round turns the suite red. No timing figure is added.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the parallel claim can fail
Before: seeded serial engineStatus: case 20 green
After: seeded serial: red; unseeded green
Method: gate - seeded control on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/engines-rules-test.cjs:254-262 (before) instant probes, `Date.now()-t0<500`
SEED_SERIAL run before: ✔ case 20 (40.8 ms)

title: codex reports codex-cli/..., a prefix the price book and registry never name
instrument: econ-rules-test case: for each real provider, the reported prefix (taken from its reported-string builder, no spawn) resolves through priceOf() to its own book entry; seed codex-cli and watch it go red
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/codex.ts reports `codex-cli/<model>`, but the registry, the price book and call.ts's timeout rows all name it `codex`. priceOf() never reaches the codex book entry, and one engine's usage rows split under two names.

## Description
priceOf() keys on the part of the reported string before "/" (desk/src/lib/engines/prices.ts:29). Six of seven providers report `<registry name>/...`. codex is the exception (codex.ts:42). A successful or exit row resolves "codex-cli", which is not in the book, so it lands in the unpriced fallback. A timeout row carries p.name "codex" (call.ts:33,45). Today both give unpriced/null, so the figures agree by accident, and a rate later set on "codex" would never apply to a successful call. econ-rules-test case e checks registered names, not reported strings, so the hand-kept list passes (§4.7). Fix options: report `codex/<model>` (codex.ts, which changes the label UAT run records quote) or alias the book. Pick one, and pin it with the instrument.

## Flow
- UAT text-live run -> codex success row provider codex-cli/gpt-6-astra -> priceOf -> "codex-cli" not in book
- same run, a timeout -> row provider "codex" -> book entry
- fix: one prefix + econ test over reported strings

## Expected impact
Usage per engine stops splitting, and a codex rate lands where it is declared. The risk is that the label in UAT reports changes if codex.ts is the side that moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one name per engine across registry, ledger and book
Before: 1 of 7 providers report a prefix outside the book; codex rows under 2 names
After: 0 of 7; 1 name
Method: probe - read every reported-string builder against PRICE_BOOK keys; the econ test that would gate it is in prices.ts/econ-rules-test.cjs, outside this round's map
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/codex.ts:42 `reported = `codex-cli/${model}``
desk/src/lib/engines/prices.ts:20 "codex" entry; :29 split("/")[0]
desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:33,45 timeout row uses p.name
tools/econ-rules-test.cjs:79-82 case e reads registeredProviders()

title: Context map omits four engine modules: call, health, meter, prices
body:
## Summary
context-map.json's engines entry lists 9 of the 13 modules in desk/src/lib/engines/. call.ts, health.ts, meter.ts and prices.ts belong to no context, and neither does tools/econ-rules-test.cjs.

## Description
The four unmapped modules hold the deadline core every engine call passes through (call.ts), the engine check (health.ts), the usage ledger (meter.ts) and the price book (prices.ts). No sweep owns them, so this round had to leave the codex price-book finding (above) as out-of-scope. The context map is edited by the director or operator only (escalation: architecture).

## Flow
- git ls-files desk/src/lib/engines -> 13 files; context-map engines file_paths -> 9
- no context lists call.ts / health.ts / meter.ts / prices.ts

## Expected impact
The next engines sweep can build in the seam that every call goes through.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every engine module has an owning context
Before: 4 of 13 modules (236 lines) and 1 suite unmapped
After: 0 of 13
Method: probe - a walk of context-map.json against git ls-files
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
wc -l: call.ts 50, health.ts 103, meter.ts 51, prices.ts 32
context-map.json engines.file_paths: codex, embed, listen, text, types, vision, voice, registry, shape, engines-rules-test

title: Vision retries without think on any failed status, doubling 404/500 calls
instrument: stubbed fetch counting POSTs per status (404 model missing, 500, 400 think rejected) plus one recorded Ollama reply for think on a non-thinking model, to pin which status the retry is for
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts retries the request without `think` after any non-ok status, not only after the rejection the retry exists for.

## Description
vision.ts:48-49: `let res = await post({...body, think:false}); if (!res.ok) res = await post(body);`. A 404 for a model that is not pulled, or a 500, sends the whole image a second time and drops the first status and body. vision.ts:4 states the purpose: retry for models that reject the think key. Narrowing it needs the status Ollama actually returns for that rejection, which this round could not record (no live calls).

## Flow
- model not pulled -> 404 -> second POST with the full image -> 404 again, ~2x latency
- fix: retry only on the think-rejection status, keep the first error otherwise

## Expected impact
A missing vision model fails in one round trip instead of two. The risk is a wrong status guess, which would stop the think fallback from firing.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one request per failure that cannot be fixed by dropping think
Before: 2 POSTs on 404/500 (read from vision.ts:48-49)
After: 1 POST predicted
Method: simulation - three walked cases (404, 500, 400 think); probe needs a recorded Ollama reply
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:48-49
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:4 "`think: false` first, retried without for models that reject the key"

title: voice.ts says listening is browser-only; listen.ts is the server path
instrument: none beyond review: a comment edit; the probe is the grep of the stale sentence against listen.ts and /api/listen
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/voice.ts:17 says "Listening is done in the browser (Web Speech) for now; a server path can come later." The server path already exists.

## Description
listen.ts is registered (listen.ts:60), served by desk/src/app/api/listen/route.ts and used by the web desk test bar (listen.ts:11). A reader who trusts voice.ts:17 misses that path, and a stale capability claim is worse than no claim. Fix: say what is true (server speech-to-text in listen.ts; the phone still listens in the browser).

## Flow
- read voice.ts header -> believe there is no server STT -> miss listen.ts

## Expected impact
Readers find the speech-to-text path. Nothing can break, because the change is a comment.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the doc states what the code does
Before: 1 stale capability sentence
After: 0
Method: probe - grep of the claim against listen.ts and api/listen; no gate sees a comment, hence B
Result: better
Gate: none

title: One engines suite process hung about 25 min under heavy load
instrument: the load23 harness (32 concurrent x N, 20 burners) with node --test-timeout and a SIGTERM handler that prints process._getActiveHandles(), to name the handle that held the process
body:
## Summary
In the Before measurement for case 23, 1 of 64 loaded runs of tools/engines-rules-test.cjs did not exit for about 25 minutes, after its tests had reported, and had to be killed.

## Description
The process (started 18:57:12) was still alive after the rest of the round ended. Its output had already reached case 23, which the harness parsed. Something kept the event loop alive. Candidates are the session store ticker cleared in after() (engines-rules-test.cjs:228), a pending stub timer, or the child spawned in case 7. run-rules would catch it only at the 600 s RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT, as a red suite.

## Flow
- load23: 32 x 2 runs beside 20 burners -> 63 exit, 1 alive at +25 min
- instrument: dump active handles on timeout

## Expected impact
If it recurs inside run-rules, it costs a 10-minute red. Naming the handle decides whether it is the suite or the machine.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every suite process exits after its last test
Before: 1 of 64 loaded runs hung (not reproduced in the 64-run After round)
After: unknown until the handle is named
Method: experiment - the same harness twice; the hang appeared once, so no deterministic rung yet
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
Get-CimInstance: PID 31580 node engines-rules-test.cjs, CreationDate 18:57:12, killed ~19:2x
load23 after: 64 of 64 exited
